items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-05-11
items.q: Manuel lived right opposite Uncle Natty's house on Erdworth Street. And I used to watch Manuel when he'd come in from work and when he'd leave.

ctx.x: Natty had to do that with Manuel Perez.

That's right. A long time. A lot of the old time teachers were that way. Well, Manuel lived right opposite Uncle Natty's house on Erdworth Street. And I used to watch Manuel when he'd come in from work and when he'd leave. In the evenings, I used to follow the parades. I used to follow the bands. That's the one that Louie came out of. I used to love to hear those kids play those horns. I'd follow them for blocks.
That's a tuxedo or the honours band.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-05-27
items.q: I followed Manuel in the parades, and sometimes I walked the parades with him

ctx.x: Well, who did you listen to come?

Well, Manuel Perez lived across the street from my grandfather, and he was part of the family. And there was another old trumpet player that I very seldom hear too much said about, George Moret. And his wife practically helped my mother to bring me up because that's how close-knit all families were here. All of the Creole families down in this area, they're close-knit. And half the time, my mother couldn't find me. I was either at Old Man Jaws Bowl by my grandfather, by Manuel Perez, all over to Bonnie's house,…
Were you any kind of Moret or Parade?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1969-12-30
items.q: Mostly like they played in Manu Perez and guys like that played practically the same type of trumpet.

ctx.x: Do you remember him as playing any jazz or remember him as a brass band? Well, yes.
Mostly like they played in Manu Perez and guys like that played practically the same type of trumpet.
Do you remember who was in George Moret's bands?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-09-18
items.q: But staying right there with Manuel Perez, Milford Piron, old man Gus Moret, and people like that, and you have to learn, otherwise you don't have nothing in your head if you can't learn with these fellas.

ctx.x: Mm-hmm. Well, you must have been an awful good soloist, changing from the rapids. There's so many things.

Well, the training that I had is responsible for it. Well, for instance, my daddy was a musician and in fact, most of my family were musicians. But staying right there with Manuel Perez, Milford Piron, old man Gus Moret, and people like that, and you have to learn, otherwise you don't have nothing in your head if you can't learn with these fellas. George Moret. Old man George Moret. Yeah.
